problem: Chip developers spend a large share of time on testing and debugging failing simulations; Silogy first offered cloud test running and now sells Viv, an AI agent that finds root causes.

technical_complexity.rationale: Understanding RTL code, logs and waveforms requires deep domain knowledge and reliable agent behavior.

defensibility.rationale: Integration into verification flows helps but large EDA vendors own the toolchains.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Synopsys and Cadence added AI debug features to Verdi and Verisium; Synopsys said in July 2026 it built an agent that can run a full verification cycle.

market_need_then: The launch post cites a claim that chip developers spend 70% of their time on testing; AI chip design interest was rising.

identity.logo: Wordmark 'SiLogy' with capital S and L

branding.brand_signature: Product persona Viv, 'Your AI Verification Engineer'

brand_strength.rationale: Name hints at silicon and logic but can be mistaken for Silimate; no press on the brand.

outcome_analysis: Silogy is an active three person YC W24 company that moved from a cloud test running tool to an AI verification agent, Viv. No funding could be verified, no exit was found, and large EDA vendors and other AI chip verification startups are active in the same wedge.
notes: The $500K pre-seed or convertible note from February or March 2024 appears only in VCBacked, CB Insights and FundedIQ aggregators and is unverified. One search summary labelled Kay Li CTO while YC says CEO. Pivot from CI tool to agent is evident from YC page versus company site but has no date. Dated competitor sources near the batch were not found.
